Galvadon is the semi-mythical last living kaleidosaur specimen on all of Azeroth, hiding somewhere in Un'Goro Crater in the Journey to Un'Goro expansion for Hearthstone. Professor Doyle, who has embarked on an expedition to Un'Goro with his assistant Eddie, is convinced that the creature exists because every other expedition ever sent to find it has disappeared, which he says is obvious proof that it must be there. Galvadon is summoned when a paladin completes the quest "The Last Kaleidosaur".

Game time usually may refer to monthly periods of a subscription to access World of Warcraft. There are various methods to purchase game time, but the most simple way is to buy it from the Battle.net Shop, the WoW Token in-game, or via the Recruit A Friend program with the Game Time (item). Other ways to obtain game time vary from purchasing a Battle.net Gift Card or a 60-Day Pre-Paid Game Card. Having a subscription or game time allows access to the retail servers up to the last expansion from the current one, Classic Era, and the Classic branch. On 25 March 2021, game time options for 30, 90 and 180 days have been removed and replaced with a 60 days option.

The World of Warcraft Game Guide was a section of the official site. It contained explanations of gameplay, features, strategy, and lore in World of Warcraft. The original version was written by Nebu, and later versions may have been as well. The Game Guide contained hundreds of pages, most of which were on generic game-play. The articles documented here are mostly the specifically unique and the lore-centric articles.

Garrisons are one of the main features of Warlords of Draenor. Garrisons are phased, highly customizable character-specific sub-zones, where players can arrange, construct and manage their own base of operations against the Iron Horde. Expansive and fully explorable areas featuring dozens of different buildings and characters, garrisons are brought to life by the player's followers, interactable NPCs who must be inspired (or bribed) to join the player's ranks. Detailed characters in their own right, followers can be grouped up and sent off to undertake quick quests, delve into dangerous dungeons or join with an army of allies to tackle special raids against mighty foes. After reaching Level 40 (100 pre-Shadowlands), characters with Level 2 or 3 garrisons will be offered Garrison Campaign quest chains every week. Sometimes the quests can result in permanent upgrades to the garrison. Completing all quest chains is necessary for The Garrison Campaign achievement. The quest chains are divided into three "parts", and you have to complete all quest chains of one part to get chains from the following parts. The quest chains in parts 1 and 2 are offered in random order, while in part 3, the quest chains are in a fixed order.

The Garad'kra is a group of Horde militias founded in the wake of the Cataclysm. Its role is to be dispersed across Kalimdor to police the territories of the Horde and maintain order in the chaos created by the Cataclysm. Its captains compared the Garad'kra to a spider and its web: if enemies approach or any damage is done to the web, the spider is able to respond with swift, precise force. New members are initiated into the Garad'kra through a ceremony in Orgrimmar's Ring of Valor, in which they swear the :Blood Oath of the Horde under a shaman's supervision. A Garrison Invasion is an event that occurs inside your garrison from time to time. After an introductory invasion triggered by questing, further invasions become available after killing enough of a certain type of enemy across . During the event, large amounts of enemies will enter the garrison and attack guards and structures. The invasion has several phases spanning about 10-15 minutes total. Success is based on a Victory Point (VP) system based on killing invaders and completing other objectives. Reaching certain VP thresholds grants up to four tiers of rewards, each of which can be earned once per week.

]] Gargons (also pluralized as gargon) are Stoneborn creatures found in Revendreth. Chiseled in the image of things that go bump in the night, these vicious quadrupeds prowl the cobblestone streets of Revendreth to maintain order, by fear or force. Gargons are crafted from stone and animated with anima. The venthyr use them as guards, pets, hunting companions, and fellow tormenters of souls. In the rare battles Revendreth has fought, gargons have been used on the front line against ground forces.
